---
title: "Sign-up Email Verification Rate"
description: "Share of email code entries that succeeded, almost all of them at sign-up."
---

The proportion of email one-time-code entries that succeeded over a selected
reporting period.

During sign-up, CanadaLogin sends a code to the new user's email address to check
that they control it. IBM Verify records this as the `email_otp` factor, but it is
not a second factor: it happens before the account exists, and nobody signs in
with it. That is why it is left out of [MFA Success Rate](mfa-success-rate.qmd)
and the other sign-in factor metrics, and measured here on its own.

A small share of `email_otp` events carry a user, so the account already existed
and they are not sign-up checks. They are most likely the same check when an
existing user changes their email address. The summary table cannot separate
them. For the
exact split, filter the raw stream on `performedby_type = 'api'`; see
[`mfa_activity`](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/mfa_activity.qmd).

## Calculation

Restrict to `mfa_type = 'email_otp'`. Divide the sum of `count` where
`result = 'success'` by the sum of `count` where `result` is `'success'` or
`'failure'`. Exclude `sent` rows from both: they are codes issued, not outcomes.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
    CAST(SUM(count) FILTER (WHERE result = 'success') AS DOUBLE)
        / NULLIF(SUM(count), 0) AS sign_up_email_verification_rate
FROM ibm_verify_events_transformed.events_mfa_activity
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE CAST(from_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
  AND mfa_type = 'email_otp'
  -- outcomes only; a "sent" row is a code issued
  AND result IN ('success', 'failure');
```

## R

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_mfa_activity")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    as.Date(from_date) <= as.Date("2026-05-28"),
    mfa_type == "email_otp",
    # outcomes only; a "sent" row is a code issued
    result %in% c("success", "failure")
  ) |>
  summarise(
    sign_up_email_verification_rate =
      sum(if_else(result == "success", as.double(count), 0), na.rm = TRUE) /
        sum(count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

The rate is a proportion between 0 and 1, counted per entry: someone who mistypes
the code once and then gets it right adds one failure and one success. It does
not count people who were sent a code and never entered one; those are sign-ups
abandoned at the email step, and show up only as `sent` rows.

## Alternative names

- email OTP success rate
- email verification success rate
- sign-up email check rate
